title: NGT vs Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)

blocks.content: The National Green Tribunal is guided by principles of natural justice and is mandated to make an endeavor for disposal of applications or appeals finally within 6 months of filing.

rows: Adjudicates environmental disputes and orders compensation
Sets environmental standards and monitors pollution levels
Principles of Natural Justice (not bound by CPC, 1908)
Administrative and technical protocols under MoEFCC
Appeals go directly to the Supreme Court of India
Decisions/orders challenged before Appellate Authorities or NGT

items: NGT does NOT have jurisdiction over the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Indian Forest Act, 1927.
CPCB derives statutory powers from two primary statutes: the Water Act, 1974 and the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981.
Appeals against the award or decision of NGT lie directly to the Supreme Court within 90 days.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established in 2010 under the NGT Act 2010 for effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection.
The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) is a statutory organization constituted in 1974 under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.
NGT is a quasi-judicial body guided by principles of natural justice, whereas CPCB is an executive technical body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
India became the third country in the world—after Australia and New Zealand—to set up a specialized environmental tribunal.
CPCB provides technical services to the Ministry and coordinates the activities of State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs).
